_comment: Every scheduled run writes one record here — including, especially, a run that could not connect. A failed run that logs is data; a failed run that stays silent is a hole in the record, and a hole is indistinguishable from a run that never fired. Record shape: { date, slot: open|hourly|preclose|retro, at, fired, connected, actions, note }. 'connected' means the brokerage connector attached and the run read live account state; a run that reasoned only from this repo's JSON is fired=true, connected=false. Per-run rows begin on recordsBeginOn. Anything earlier is carried in priorSummary as an aggregate, because those runs predate this file and the per-run detail was never written down. Do not backfill it.

scheduler.note: True as of 2026-08-05, and read it narrowly. This is a desktop scheduled task, not a server-side runner — it fires only while the operator's Claude app is open, so a missed window runs late on next launch rather than on time. Every run therefore checks how late it fired and refuses to write an order specification if the quotes it would rest on are stale. On 2026-08-05 all nine rows fired inside their own windows, four to seven minutes late, so the guard was never the thing that stopped a run — but one clean day is one clean day, not a server. The example this note used to cite, a retro slot of 16:30 ET firing at 00:45 ET, was removed with the test rows on 8/5 and is described here rather than pointed at, because the file no longer contains it. 'Configured' means a trigger exists and has fired, not that the four slots fire reliably at their stated times.

slots.name: Market open
slots.does: Verify the connector attached before reasoning about anything. Check settled cash, apply exit rules, run the six-item pre-trade checklist.

slots.name: Mid-session
slots.does: Enforce exits the hour a level is hit. Default is no trade.

slots.name: Pre-close
slots.does: Exit discipline. Decide overnight holds explicitly rather than by default. Close option no-fly windows.

slots.name: Retro
slots.does: Read-only. Grades the day against the rules outcome-blind, then runs the standing rule-drift check. Never places an order.

Fired 15:21 ET against the 15:17 slot, four minutes late, inside the guard with live quotes struck 19:22:16 UTC. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. One position, the operator's 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls at a 0.57 average, bid 0.47 against a 0.49 ask. All four levels checked against that bid and none is hit: target 0.684 needs the bid up 45.5%, the 0.342 stop needs it down 27.2%, the position is at -17.5% on the bid and -15.8% on the 0.48 mark, the time stop is 8/13 with today session one of five, and the no-fly window was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 1,518 events across 8/6 to 8/15 and SMR appears in none, so nothing prints before the 8/14 expiry. Four levels, four clear. Last hour's gain was handed back within the hour and by the exact mechanism last hour flagged as the fragile one: implied volatility fell 102.1% to 96.2%, and at a 0.0055 vega those 5.9 points are about -0.033 of contract, with the underlying down 9.46 to 9.36 bid contributing about -0.051 at a 0.51 delta. A gain that had to be sold to be kept was not sold and did not keep. The finding of this run is not a level, it is the gate. The expiry item has been handed to the 15:33 pre-close for five consecutive hours on the understanding that the pre-close would exit or record an exception; this run tested that assumption instead of passing it on, by running scripts/validate.mjs against a maximally correct sell-to-close spec for the contract actually held. It fails on two independent counts, both reproducible. The 21-day expiry floor is applied to any spec with kind option regardless of action, so an exit from a 7-day contract is refused on the ground that the contract is too short-dated to buy - the rule the exit exists to honour is the rule that blocks it. The affordability check computes limit x qty x 100 and charges it against deployable cash regardless of action, so a sell-to-close that raises 96.00 is refused for costing 96.00 against 11.98. Both are entry rules applied to an exit, and together they mean this project cannot publish an option exit specification at all - not this one, any of them. That is escalated to the operator rather than fixed here: the rule-drift policy reserves rule changes to the operator, and an agent that may decide for itself that a loosening is really a correction has no gate. No spec published, so no order specification exists for the pre-close to inherit. Nothing is lost operationally that was not already the case - every exit in this project has always required a human to execute, so the recommendation reaches the operator through the board and this note. What is lost is the gated, machine-checked form of it. No new entry: deployable settled cash is 11.98 for a sixth hour and buys no contract, and the mid-session bar is higher than the open's in any case.

Fired 15:36 ET against the 15:33 slot, three minutes late, well inside the staleness guard, on quotes struck 19:35:52-19:35:55 UTC. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly against the connector's list; every other account was discarded unread. One position, the operator's 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls at a 0.57 average, bid 0.47 against a 0.51 ask. Every check this slot owes was run and written down. Option no-fly: re-pulled live rather than carried forward, 1,517 earnings events across 8/6-8/14 with SMR in none of them, so no print lands before the 8/14 expiry. Earnings tonight on the underlying: none, so no straddle is owed and the no-straddle-no-hold rule is satisfied by the absence of an event rather than by an exception to it. Levels: target 0.684 needs the bid up 45.5%, the 0.342 stop needs it down 27.2%, the position is -17.5% on the bid and -14.0% on the 0.49 mark, time stop 8/13 with today session one of five. Four levels, four clear. The thing that triggered is not a level. The rulebook forbids holding an option into its final week, and 8/14 is 8 days out today and 7 tomorrow, so that week opens at tomorrow's bell and this was the last run able to act inside the rule - which is why five hourly runs handed the item here rather than acting. Theta -0.0338 a day is 6.9% of mark, break-even 9.99 against a 9.39 underlying needs +6.4% in six sessions, so the rule is right about this contract specifically and not merely in general. The exit is due, and it could not be published. This run reproduced the 15:21 finding rather than inheriting it, by running scripts/validate.mjs against a maximally correct sell-to-close built from the open position itself - broker instrument id, live 0.47/0.51 quote, 791 open interest, delta 0.4997, limit 0.49 at the mark - and it fails on exactly two counts: the 21-day expiry floor, applied to any option spec regardless of action, refuses the exit for being too short-dated to buy, and the limit x qty x 100 affordability charge refuses a sell that raises 98.00 for costing 98.00 against 11.98 deployable. Both are entry rules applied to an exit, so no option exit is publishable in this project at all. Not fixed here: the mandate forbids weakening the validator and the drift policy reserves rule changes to the operator, which is exactly the rule an unattended run publishing straight to live should not be the one to bend. Escalated with the reproduction attached. The consequence is recorded plainly rather than softened: the position is held overnight and is in breach of the final-week rule from tomorrow's open, held because the exit had no publishable form and not because the hold was judged the better trade. No new entry - the daily mandate binds the open slot, this slot may not open a position in the last thirty minutes, and 11.98 deployable buys no contract for a seventh consecutive read. moves.json pruned: the 8/5 earnings cluster removed as a day behind, the UPST 8/11 time stop removed as a clock on a position that closed 8/5, the SMR 8/14 expiry added as the next dated thing that acts on the account, and spot refreshed from live bids on every surviving row - OKLO alone had drifted 2.5% from the reference price it was carrying.
